To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the spectral reflectance of the ocean surface is dominated by whitecaps, which are highly variable and difficult to predict; (2) the reflectance of the water column is dominated by phytoplankton absorption, which can be predicted with a high degree of accuracy using the absorption coefficients of phytoplankton and the concentration of chlorophyll; and (3) the reflectance at the sea surface and in the water column is highly correlated, and this correlation is useful for predicting

(a) the optical properties of the water are affected by the presence of the phytoplankton and (b) the optical properties are affected by the light field, and in turn, the light field is affected by the presence and distribution of the phytoplanks.
